keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 454-472, a period Cliopatria lacks (its Gepid row starts 510). The Gepids page: 'Ardaric established an independent Gepid kingdom following the Hunnic defeat at the Battle of Nedao' (454; the battle was in Pannonia 'in 454 or 455'), and the kingdom 'covered a large part of the former Roman province of Dacia, north of the Danube'. Drawn as the Cliopatria 510 heartland: 125,235 km2 (495 cells). The huns dossier (eu-06-a) hands the Gepids all of Dacia (Banat, Crisana, Transylvania, Transcarpathia, Muntenia, Oltenia, 986 cells, about 249,000 km2) on the strength of a Jordanes line quoted from the same page; this dossier keeps to the page's 'large part' and the Cliopatria extent, so 483 of those cells are not drawn here.

keyframe_review.note: 151,898 km2 (581 cells) for 510-545, Romania, Hungary and Serbia, 18.8-24.95 E, 43.4-48.0 N. The shape holds Sirmium (12 cells of a 40 km disc) and a 74-cell strip of the south Danube bank round Singidunum that the Eastern Roman Empire's 509 shape also holds. The Gepids page has them expelled from Sirmium in 504 and 'settling in the rich area around Singidunum' only 'after 537'; the Cunimund page has Sirmium Gepid 'since 536'. The correction is therefore the heartland alone for 510-535; 536-545 are the next two keyframes. No infobox area on the page, so no area comparison.

The Cunimund page: 'The Gepids had held Sirmium since 536, after taking it from the Byzantine emperor Justinian I'; the Thurisind page dates 'the takeover by the Gepids of the formerly Roman city of Sirmium in 537'. One year apart; 536 is used.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 539-545: the Cliopatria 510 shape as drawn, with the Singidunum strip. 'The Gepids reached the height of their power after 537, settling in the rich area around Singidunum'; 'In 539, most of the Byzantine army was in Persia, so the Gepids and Heruls plundered Moesia' and 'the Romans were forced to pay heavy taxes and recognize new zones of Gepid occupation'.

151,784 km2, the same extent. Thurisind (c. 548-560) 'was crushed in the decisive battle of the Asfeld held west of Sirmium' in 552; the Thurisind page names Gepidia as 'located in Central Europe' and puts Dacia ripensis and Singidunum in Gepid hands. The shape holds.

131,448 km2 in Cliopatria's 555 shape, 134,230 km2 with Syrmia: the south bank of the Danube (74 cells, 18,700 km2) drops out. No page opened (Gepids, Cunimund, Thurisind, Pannonian Avars, Singidunum) moves the Danube bank in 555 or dates a Byzantine recovery of Singidunum (the Singidunum page has 'Justinian I rebuilt Singidunum from scratch in 535' and 'the Byzantines recaptured it in 596'), so that drop is Cliopatria's unverified reading, kept as drawn and recorded at confidence 1. Review fix: Cliopatria also moves 11 cells, Syrmia with Sirmium itself (19.2-20.1 E, 44.8-45.2 N, 2,782 km2), from the Gepids to the Lombards in 555 with no event. The Cunimund page, re-read 2026-10-20: 'The Gepids had held ... Sirmium ... since 536, after taking it from the Byzantine emperor Justinian I' and 'the Gepid king handed Sirmium over to the Byzantines' (Cunimund died 567). The cells stay Gepid to 567, so the capital lies inside the state and the 567 loss to the Eastern Roman Empire hands over land the keyframes hold. The 11 cells are the intersection of the Lombard 555 and Gepid 546 shapes.

ledger.note: 454: Ardaric founds the Gepid kingdom in the lands of the Danube and the Tisza after the Hunnic defeat at Nedao. 'Ardaric established an independent Gepid kingdom following the Hunnic defeat at the Battle of Nedao' (infobox 454); the battle was fought 'in Pannonia in 454 or 455', so the year is the page's with a one-year doubt. The page gives the land as 'a large part of the former Roman province of Dacia, north of the Danube'; the region is the Cliopatria 510 heartland (the researcher's reading).
473: the Gepids take Sirmium. 'After the Ostrogoths left Pannonia in 473, the Gepids captured Sirmium.'

504: Theodoric's comes Pitzia takes Sirmium. 'Comes Pitzia expelled the Gepid troops from Sirmium without much resistance.' The Ostrogothic Kingdom page puts the campaign in 504-505 and calls it the recovery of Pannonia and Sirmium; the Theodoric page: 'In 504-505, Theodoric extended his realms in the Balkans by defeating the Gepids.'

536: the Gepids take Sirmium from the Byzantines. 'The Gepids had held Sirmium since 536, after taking it from the Byzantine emperor Justinian I.' The Thurisind page has 'the takeover by the Gepids of the formerly Roman city of Sirmium in 537'. The Ostrogothic Kingdom held Sirmium from 504-505 on the pages opened and the Gothic War page does not say how it passed to Justinian; the counterpart is the page's own (eastern-roman-empire), and the Ostrogothic dossier records its side at confidence 1.

region.text: the south bank of the Danube from Singidunum to Ratiaria (Dacia ripensis), the 'new zones of Gepid occupation'

ledger.note: 539: the Gepids hold the Danube bank round Singidunum. 'The Gepids reached the height of their power after 537, settling in the rich area around Singidunum'; 'In 539 ... the Gepids and Heruls plundered Moesia' and 'the Romans were forced to pay heavy taxes and recognize new zones of Gepid occupation.' The Thurisind page lists 'the loss to the Gepids of Dacia ripensis (Serbia) and Singidunum'. The page does not date the recognition; 539 is the year of the plundering and the strip is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the south bank of the Danube from Singidunum to Ratiaria

ledger.note: 555: the Gepids lose the Danube bank round Singidunum in Cliopatria's data. Nothing on the Gepids, Cunimund, Thurisind or Pannonian Avars pages moves it; the Eastern Roman Empire dossier records the mirror gain at confidence 1. Page silent; the year is Cliopatria's shape change. Singidunum page (read 2026-10-20): Gepids at Singidunum in 488, 'Justinian I rebuilt Singidunum from scratch in 535', 'the Byzantines recaptured it in 596'; it dates no Byzantine return in 555.

region.text: the western Gepid lands between the Danube and the Tisza that the Lombards took in 567

ledger.note: 565: war with the Lombards breaks out again. 'Open war with the Lombards, now led by Alboin, began again in 565' (Cunimund page); the Alboin page: 'in 565, a new war erupted with the Gepids' and the Lombards 'suffered a complete defeat' when Justin II sent Baduarius (565 or 566). The zone is the part of the Gepid land the Lombards hold in Cliopatria's 567 shape.

region.text: the western Gepid lands taken by the Lombards

ledger.note: 567: the war ends with the Gepids beaten. 'the Lombards soundly defeated Cunimund's forces in 567'; the Alboin page: Alboin killed Cunimund and the allied Avars overran the Gepids.

region.text: the western Gepid lands, between the Danube and the Tisza

ledger.note: 567: the Lombards take the western Gepid lands. 'the Lombards soundly defeated Cunimund's forces in 567'. The region is the overlap of Cliopatria's Lombard 567 and Gepid 566 shapes (110 cells); the Lombards held it only until their departure for Italy in 568.

region.text: the Gepid lands east of the Tisza and in Transylvania taken by the Avars

ledger.note: 567: the Avars overrun the rest of the Gepid kingdom. 'In 567 the Avars formed an alliance with the Lombards ... together they destroyed much of the Gepid kingdom'; the Gepids page: 'finally overrun by the Avars in the 567 Lombard-Gepid war'. The region is the overlap of Cliopatria's Avar 567 and Gepid 566 shapes (386 cells).

567: Sirmium passes to the Byzantines. The Cunimund page: Cunimund promised Sirmium to Justin II 'in return for help, and later handed the city over to the Byzantines'; it also says the Byzantine troops kept Sirmium. The page gives no year; the Eastern Roman Empire dossier dates the return 567, which this entry follows (confidence 1). The Pannonian Avars page has Sirmium captured by the Avars by 582. Sirmium and the 11 cells of Syrmia stay in the Gepid shape to 567 (review fix 2026-10-20), so this loss and the dissolve hand over land the keyframes hold.

region.text: the Gepid kingdom's last shape with Syrmia and Sirmium, split between the Avars, the Lombards and the Byzantines (Sirmium)

ledger.note: 567: the Gepid kingdom is destroyed. 'The Gepids were finally overrun by the Avars in the 567 Lombard-Gepid war'; infobox end 567; Cunimund 'Died: 567'. 'Many Gepids followed Alboin to Italy in 568 ... but many remained in the area of their old kingdom.'

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: The Germanic peoples under Ardaric defeated the sons of Attila; Ardaric founded the Gepid kingdom.
wars.note: 'The decisive battle was fought at the (unidentified) Nedao River' in Pannonia 'in 454 or 455'.

wars.name: Ostrogothic recovery of Sirmium
wars.outcome: Theodoric's comes Pitzia expelled the Gepid troops from Sirmium and the Ostrogoths 'recovered Pannonia' (504-505).
wars.note: The Theodoric the Great page also dates 'defeating the Gepids' to 504-505 and credits Theodoric with the province of Pannonia.

wars.name: Gepid-Byzantine conflict over Sirmium and Moesia

zones.text: the south Danube bank round Singidunum

wars.outcome: The Gepids took Sirmium (536/537) and in 539 plundered Moesia; the Romans paid and 'recognize[d] new zones of Gepid occupation'.
wars.note: Thurisind page: 'Sirmium's takeover was followed in 539 by a bloody confrontation between the Gepids and the Byzantines'. The Gepids page also has Justinian's army 'routed along the way by the Heruli'.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid war (549-552)
wars.outcome: The Lombards, allied with Justinian from 551, 'inflicted a disastrous defeat on the Gepids at the Battle of Asfeld in 552'; Thurisind lost his eldest son Turismod. No border moved.
wars.note: Cunimund page: 'By 549, the Gepids were at war with the Lombards.' The battle was 'west of Sirmium'. The Alboin page dates Asfeld 552.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid war (565-567)
wars.outcome: Alboin's Lombards and the Avars destroyed the Gepid kingdom in 567; Cunimund was killed and the Avars took the Gepid lands.
wars.note: Alboin page: the Avar alliance of 566; 'In 567 the allies made their final move against Cunimund'; the Avars demanded 'all of the lands held by the Gepids'.

certainty.note: A tribal kingdom on the Danube and Tisza plains; the frontier with the Eastern Roman Empire on the Danube is approximate and its position round Singidunum changes with the wars.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Kingdom of the Gepids' 510-566 (four shapes). This dossier starts the state in 454 (Nedao, Gepids page) and ends it in 567 (page), adding five keyframes the data lacks (454-509, 536-545 split) and moving the Cliopatria 510 shape to 510-535 minus Sirmium and the south Danube bank. Mismatch with the huns dossier (eu-06-a): its 454 losses to kingdom-of-the-gepids are the whole of Dacia (Banat, Crisana, Transylvania, Transcarpathia, Muntenia, Oltenia: 986 cells) plus the Danube-Tisza interfluve, 483 cells more than the heartland drawn here; the Gepids page opened here says 'a large part of the former Roman province of Dacia', and the Cliopatria shape (581 cells) is the heartland. A gap-filler should decide whether the 483 cells (chiefly Muntenia and Oltenia) belong to the Gepids, to nobody or to the Huns. Sirmium: the Ostrogothic Kingdom dossier holds it 504/505-535; here the Gepids take it from Justinian in 536 (Cunimund page; Thurisind page 537) and give it to the Byzantines at an undated point (the Eastern Roman Empire dossier has 567). The eastern-roman-empire dossier has no Sirmium event between 505 and 567 and none for the Singidunum strip before 510; eu-05 should reconcile. The Danube bank (Singidunum to Ratiaria, 74 cells) is in Cliopatria's Gepid shape from 510 and in the Eastern Roman Empire's 509 shape too; the pages put the Gepids at Singidunum only after 537 (539 recognition), so it is drawn Gepid 539-554 only, and its 555 drop is unverified (page silent). Capitals: Sirmium (infobox 'Sirmium'), held 473-504 and from 536; no page names a capital for 454-472 or 505-535. Rulers: only Thurisind and Cunimund have page dates; Ardaric (454), Thraustila (489) and Thrasaric (504) are named without reigns. Page budget: Gepids, Cunimund, Thurisind, Pannonian Avars (four of five). Review fix 2026-10-20 (reviewer eu-06-e): Syrmia with Sirmium (11 cells, 2,782 km2) is kept in the Gepid shape 555-567 and the dissolve region, against Cliopatria's 555 hand-over to the Lombards; the Lombards dossier removes the same cells (S = intersect of Lombards 555 and Gepids 546). Pages opened for the thin findings: Singidunum (no date for a Byzantine recovery before 596; the 555 loss of the Danube bank stays Cliopatria's, confidence 1) and Ardaric (no seat named, so no capital for 454-472 or 505-535). Eastern Roman Empire (eu-05) gains Sirmium at 567 with a 25 km radius, this ledger loses it with 40 km.
